To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Geldart classification can be used to describe the fluidisation of nanoparticle agglomerates, and that the agglomerates can be described using a single parameter, the agglomerate density.
fluidisation of nanoparticle agglomerates can be explained in terms of a modified Geldart classification that accounts for multiple scale fluidization.

fluidization of nanoparticle assemblies can be achieved by using the right combination of particle and fluid properties, and that the fluidization behavior is different than that for larger particles, due to a different balance of the forces involved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fluidisation of nanoparticle assemblies.

the study of the fluidisation of nanoparticle clusters and agglomerates and the development of a new classification scheme for the Geldart diagram to account for the multiple scale fluidisation behaviour of nanoparticle assemblies.
the development of a new generation of fluidisation models that will be able to describe the behaviour of fluidised beds of fine and ultrafine particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the short range surface forces are dominant in the sub micron particle size regime and long range forces are dominant in larger particle size regime.
the fluidisation phenomenon is a function of the balance between the short range particle surface forces and the long range body forces.
fluidisation is a phenomenon which is best explained by balancing the short range particle surface active forces and the long range body forces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new classification scheme for fluidising powders based upon the particle scale forces.
for the Geldart classification of powders, the fluidisation regime is best described by the balance of the short range forces and the long range forces.
the fluidisation of nanoparticle assemblies is a function of the relative magnitude of the short and long range inter particle forces and the fluid forces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the nanoscale range the short range forces are dominant and the interstitial fluid drag forces are negligible.

in the sub millimetre size range, the fluid drag forces can be of the same order of magnitude as the immersed weight of the particle and the balance of forces is determined by the relative magnitude of the particle surface forces.

the fluidisation of nanoparticle agglomerates and aggregates are dominated by the interstitial fluid forces, but the fluidisation of the clusters and the agglomerates themselves is dominated by the short range forces.
